summary: Iteration 194 tested the DB-audit fixes C1-C7, the catalog guest fix and the load script. Everything ran only in isolated, disposable DBs. The customer DB and jeelive.ai were not touched, and nothing was deployed. New backend suite tests/db_audit_iso194.py passed 71/71. C1 AdmissionGate was unit-tested with a fake app and then through the real app. 20 auth bursts all return 200 with peak <= limit; in_flight returns to 0 and waited = 16. With a short wait, 4 succeed and 6 get 503 capacity_busy with Retry-After 2 after about 0.15 s. Cancelled waiters leave the queue and leak no slot. A waiter that was handed a slot and then cancelled keeps the slot and releases it: on Python 3.11, wait_for returns the result when the future is already done. The read and asset lanes reject immediately and never wait. The queue cap of limit*64 works: 30 immediate 503s plus 256 waited-then-503. The live lane waits. Defaults are auth 6 s and live 3 s. Real app: 50 parallel sign-ups all returned 200 in 0.42 s; the auth lane peaked at 4, waited 46, rejected 0, and in_flight ended at 0. C6: all 50 new rows have _id == id, and sign-in, Change PIN, Forgot PIN and sign-in with the reset PIN all work. C2: the owner's practice cohort returns 'unavailable' with the staff reason, record() returns False, no staff entry is written, and the student's cohort is recorded. The migration, via the real library.run_cleanups(), deletes only the staff entry, sets dirty and a new generation on the affected cohort only, and writes state done; a second run_once is a no-op. C3: a duplicate-id unique index on tejas_ledgers fails, but indexes() completes; INDEX_PROBLEMS records the failure, later indexes (users email_1) are still built, and the integrity report includes index_problems. C4: a normal open_time save moves the paper window (revision 2). A paper changed between read and write gets 409 'changed while saving'; the concurrent title change and the old window are kept and the series config is unchanged. Reload and save again returns 200. Shrinking days still unassigns the paper (moved 1). C7: anon/reviewer/student get 401/403. Prefixes '+916' and '+915…' and an old created_after get 422; an integer created_after is accepted. The dry run is the default and reports would_remove 50/5. A real run without confirm or with the wrong confirm gets 422. The confirmed run removes 50 accounts, 5 attempts, every by-user collection (5 each), cohort entries and sessions (>= 50); cohorts are marked dirty, and an audit row is written. Another prefix and an older same-prefix account are untouched (before/after counts equal). A removed session gets 401 and a removed number cannot sign in. A second run removes 0. The bridge end-to-end run of tools/load_live.py (stages 20,60) gave all 200/202, signup p95 0.27/0.85 s and 0 errors. The cleanup then removed exactly those 80 load accounts with 80 attempts, ledgers, sessions, jobs and cohort entries, and an orphan scan found no attempt_id or user_id leftovers. Regressions run on their own: forgot_pin_iso184 53/53, typed_delete_iso185 54/54, override_guard_iso192 31/31, override_all_iso193 31/31. When all four ran in parallel, iso192 and iso185 failed with database_busy/contention (harness-only; both pass solo). UI was tested with local Playwright (tests/ui194.py; public preview frontend with /api routed to bridge 127.0.0.1:8772): 24/24 at 1920 and 390. Guest Home makes no /catalog/exams or /auth/refresh call, and signed-in Home calls /catalog/exams. Sign-up succeeds after an injected 503 (2 requests). Start a test succeeds after an injected 503 and lands on /attempts/. An injected 429 on sign-in is not retried and shows 'Too many attempts…'. Forgot PIN succeeds after one 503; with 4 x 503 it makes exactly 4 tries, shows the busy message, re-enables the button, and the next tap succeeds. Sign-in with the new PIN works, and there is no horizontal overflow.

minor.issue: The new 409 CAS is raised mid-loop, after earlier papers were already re-windowed or unassigned (unassign_set). The series config is not saved yet, so a 409 can leave some papers on the new times while the config still has the old times. 'Reload and save again' fixes it, but if the owner walks away, papers and config disagree. Fix: check all rows first, or wrap the updates in a transaction.
solutions.create_index x3 in server.py and the structure.py indexes (sections unique, etc.) are not wrapped in _Safe. A failing index there can still stop startup, which C3 aimed to prevent.

action_items: Optional: make series update_config all-or-nothing (pre-check revisions or use a transaction) so a 409 never leaves papers partially moved.
Optional: wrap the server.py lifespan solutions indexes and structure.seed indexes in db._Safe (or move them into db.indexes()).

Before the live load test: uvicorn runs without --forwarded-allow-ips, so request.client.host is the ingress IP (private). The per-IP sign-up limit (60/15 min, global IPs only) will not trigger from one load machine; the per-number limit still applies. That per-IP limit is effectively off in production (pre-existing).
critical_code_review_comments: admission.wait_slot: on Python 3.11, asyncio.wait_for swallows a cancel that arrives after the slot was handed over and returns True. The request then proceeds and releases normally, so no leak (verified). The BaseException branch covers 3.12 behaviour.

cohorts.record/read and remove_staff_entries treat every tejas_users id as staff. Today only owner and reviewer live in tejas_users, so this is correct. If students are ever stored there, filtering by role in ('owner','reviewer') would be safer.

qa_cleanup leaves the tejas_phone_limits counters (they expire by TTL) and cohort snapshots (rebuilt because the cohorts are marked dirty). This is acceptable. jobs are removed by user_id only, and the orphan scan found no payload.attempt_id leftovers.
load_live.py watchdog leaves signup/signin out of the abort ratio. If sign-ups fail, the stage still continues, so read the signup bad_pct in the stage report.

postWhenFree backoff with Retry-After 2: about 2-3 s, 4-5 s and 6-7 s, so about 15 s worst case before the busy message. The UI keeps the button disabled with a spinner and re-enables it afterwards (verified).
